## How to use this

The three exercises from Lecture 26, solved. Your versions may differ in names
and layout and still be right: the checks are what matter.

::: {.notes}
Posted after class.
:::

## Set up {.smaller}

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lintr)
library(biometrydata)

avo <- avonet
```

## Restyle the hawks {.smaller}

```{r}
hawks <- avo |>
  filter(Family1 == "Accipitridae")
mean_hawk_mass <- mean(hawks$Mass, na.rm = TRUE)
habitat_summary <- hawks |>
  group_by(Habitat) |>
  summarise(mean_mass = mean(Mass),
            mean_wing = mean(Wing.Length))

nrow(hawks)
mean_hawk_mass
habitat_summary
```

## Restyle the hawks: the lint check {.smaller}

The same code, given to `lint()` as text. Your `lint("hawks.R")` should also
come back empty.

```{r}
clean <- 'hawks <- avo |>
  filter(Family1 == "Accipitridae")
mean_hawk_mass <- mean(hawks$Mass, na.rm = TRUE)
habitat_summary <- hawks |>
  group_by(Habitat) |>
  summarise(mean_mass = mean(Mass),
            mean_wing = mean(Wing.Length))
'
lint(text = clean)
```

If `lint()` says "Missing terminal newline", put the cursor after the last line
of your file and press Enter.

## Bobwhite, one column per year {.smaller}

```{r}
bw_wide <- bobwhite_counts |>
  select(route, year, count) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = count)

dim(bw_wide)
sum(is.na(bw_wide))
bw_wide[1:4, 1:6]
```

The wide version is easier to read and shows the gaps. `glmer()` needs the long
version, with year and count as variables.

## Bobwhite: for anyone fast {.smaller}

```{r}
# back to long: every empty cell becomes a row, unless you drop them
bw_wide |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -route, names_to = "year", values_to = "count") |>
  nrow()
bw_wide |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -route, names_to = "year", values_to = "count",
               values_drop_na = TRUE) |>
  nrow()

# without route, nothing identifies a row: one row of list-columns, and a warning
bobwhite_counts |>
  select(year, count) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = count) |>
  dim()
```

That "not uniquely identified" warning almost always means an ID column is
missing.

## The most pointed wings {.smaller}

```{r}
avo |>
  # Group the species by family
  group_by(Family1) |>
  # Keep families with at least 10 species
  filter(n() >= 10) |>
  # Average each family's hand-wing index
  summarise(mean_hwi = mean(Hand.Wing.Index, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  # Sort from most to least pointed
  arrange(desc(mean_hwi))
```

Swifts first, hummingbirds second, penguins last.
